planAuthority.rule: Rust backend business logic owns the canonical plan catalog, permission set, price, billing cycle, promotion, ranking offset, and active flag. Subscription and UI consume versioned projections; they do not invent or mutate a parallel catalog.
currentDrift: canonical plans and wallet_plan_assignments remain in the backend
subscription service creates subscription_plans at process start
content/static/canned frontend plans form additional divergent projections

ownershipRules.rule: Public callers may read only active public plan projections; all subscription state requires a verified principal.
User list/detail/cancel/switch/current-access derive wallet/user identity from the verified JWT and include it in every database predicate; body or path owner identifiers are never authoritative.
Non-owner subscription identifiers return the same 404 as missing identifiers and do not reveal existence.
Admin subscription reads require admin:payments:view; mutations require admin:payments:manage; plan reads/mutations require admin:plans:read/manage.
Internal activation accepts only authenticated payment-service events whose verified wallet and plan projection match the immutable payment record.

idempotencyRules.rule: A unique finalized-payment identity (chain_id, transaction_hash, log_index) can activate or extend access exactly once.
Each external mutation carries Idempotency-Key plus canonical request hash; same key/same hash replays the stored response and same key/different hash returns 409.
Lifecycle transition and outbox append commit in one local transaction; consumers record event_id before applying entitlement effects.
Cancel, expire, grant, revoke, switch, and reconciliation transitions are monotonic or valid state-machine moves and are safe under retries.
Retryable dependency failures retain pending work with bounded backoff and a dead-letter/reconciliation path; they never return a false active/success result.

allowedTransitions: active->active on one verified renewal extension
active->cancel_at_period_end on owner cancellation when paid access remains
active->cancelled on authorized immediate administrative cancellation
active->grace_period at period end when configured
active|grace_period->suspended on explicit administrative risk action
suspended->active only through an audited authorized recovery
forbiddenTransitions: cancelled|expired->active without a new verified cause
same payment identity extending more than once
switch leaving two effective subscription plans or no effective plan after a reported success
lifecycleStateMachine.autoRenewPolicy: false until a separately designed and authorized payment mandate exists; source behavior is manual repayment

activeSubscriptionPolicy.rule: A wallet has at most one effective active subscription-plan assignment at a time. Historical cancelled/expired rows remain append-only. Enterprise/manual/system grants may overlap only through an explicit plan-category policy and deterministic best-access selection.
databaseProofRequired: partial unique or exclusion constraint for effective subscription category

statusSemantics.envelope: one versioned ApiResponse compatibility adapter until all source callers migrate; internal service DTOs remain explicit and never silently change status/envelope

uiStateRules.rule: Public plans render live loading, non-empty, honest empty, error, and retry states; static/canned tiers are fixture-only.
Authenticated current-access failure is distinct from no plan; free-tier fallback must not convert dependency or authorization errors into authoritative access.
Checkout carries immutable plan_id/price-version and displays pending finality, confirmed activation, replay-safe retry, cancellation, and terminal failure.
Owner and admin subscription tables bind live BFF data and provide loading, empty, error, retry, pagination, forbidden, conflict, and mutation-in-progress states.

durableStateDependencies: versioned canonical plan catalog and price snapshot
subscription lifecycle rows with normalized owner and effective period
entitlement and ranking projection with cause/event identity

select one source of record across subscriptions and wallet_plan_assignments and document category overlap semantics
snapshot counts and invalid/duplicate owner-plan/payment identities without changing rows
backfill normalized owners, plan versions, periods, payment causes, and state history in restartable batches
quarantine ambiguous rows instead of inventing entitlement or payment proof
dual-read/shadow-compare active plan, expiry, ranking offset, and permissions per wallet
reconcile payments-to-subscriptions-to-entitlements with deterministic discrepancy classes
enable constraints only after zero unexplained conflicts and retain rollback projection

schedulerOutboxRules.rule: Expiry workers claim due rows with a lease or SKIP LOCKED, transition in a transaction, append outbox, and tolerate duplicate/crashed runs.
Outbox publication has observable lag/retry/dead-letter metrics and never marks delivered before the broker/consumer contract is satisfied.
Entitlement grant/revoke consumers are idempotent; reconciliation repairs missed delivery without extending billing periods.

outbox or entitlement lag exceeds the agreed SLO
actions: stop new mutation traffic to the Rust subscription service

blockers.summary: Public plan DTOs and live rendering do not match the pinned client contract.
blockers.resolution: Expose the canonical active PublicPlan projection through a versioned compatibility route and bind the page to it.

blockers.summary: Current access, owner list, and owner expiry/detail contracts are absent or unscoped.
blockers.resolution: Implement JWT-derived owner projections and source-compatible adapters with foreign-as-missing behavior.

blockers.summary: The gateway authenticates subscription mutations but the service trusts caller owner fields and selects by id alone.
blockers.resolution: Verify service identity/JWT context and include canonical owner in every user query and mutation predicate.

blockers.summary: Creating a subscription activates it without verified payment finality.
blockers.resolution: Create pending state or accept an authenticated finalized-payment event and activate only after A6 proof.

blockers.summary: Checkout/pay intents carry no durable plan price version or subscription activation cause.
blockers.resolution: Bind pay intent to immutable plan/price/owner data and publish verified activation identity after finality.

blockers.summary: Prefixes, methods, bodies, envelopes, fields, and success statuses drift across source client, gateway, BFF, and service.
blockers.resolution: Publish exact versioned DTO/status tables and compatibility adapters, then pass route and contract fixtures.

blockers.summary: The backend, subscription service, content files, and admin sample UI can each describe different plans; frontend compatibility producers are absent and the public page fails closed rather than presenting an unowned catalog.
blockers.resolution: Keep plan/permission/ranking business authority in Rust backend and make every other store a versioned projection.

blockers.summary: Upgrade preview and plan switch are missing in the target.
blockers.resolution: Implement owner-scoped preview and one-transaction switch using canonical prices and deterministic proration.

blockers.summary: Cancel lacks owner/admin distinction, reason/audit, conflict rules, and source response parity.
blockers.resolution: Define immediate versus period-end cancellation, enforce owner or admin permission, append audit/outbox, and preserve response semantics.

blockers.summary: There is no proven renewal, grace, expiry, revoke, or scheduler lifecycle.
blockers.resolution: Preserve manual repayment semantics, calculate periods deterministically, and add a leased idempotent expiry/revoke worker.

blockers.summary: Neither the target nor the source UNIQUE(wallet,plan) proves at most one effective subscription plan under concurrency.
blockers.resolution: Define category overlap policy, add partial/exclusion constraints, and prove concurrent create/switch behavior.

blockers.summary: Subscription transitions do not durably grant or revoke permission entitlements.
blockers.resolution: Emit transactional lifecycle events and apply idempotent cause-linked entitlement grants/revokes with reconciliation.

blockers.summary: Identity fail-closes ranking access until an authoritative entitlement projection is wired; analytics queries the identity authority rather than manufacturing a plan offset.
blockers.resolution: Serve ranking offset from the authoritative entitlement projection and distinguish unavailable from free/no-plan.

blockers.summary: A3.7 removed startup DDL into an additive candidate migration, but no runner, version ledger, baseline adoption, populated upgrade, lifecycle constraints, or reconciliation is proven.
blockers.resolution: Add the reviewed runner and ledger, inventory/backfill existing records, quarantine ambiguity, then validate lifecycle constraints and reconciliation.

blockers.summary: No activation replay key, mutation idempotency record, or transactional switch/renewal proof exists.
blockers.resolution: Add payment-cause uniqueness, request-hash idempotency, transactional state changes, and crash/replay tests.

blockers.summary: Cross-service payment/subscription/entitlement effects have no proven outbox, inbox, retry, dead-letter, or reconciliation path.
blockers.resolution: Commit lifecycle+outbox locally, consume idempotently, expose lag/failure metrics, and ship deterministic reconciliation.

blockers.summary: Admin BFF/UI omit source CRUD and use raw/static data with inconsistent response statuses.
blockers.resolution: Implement permission-scoped live list/detail/create/update/cancel and plan CRUD with loading/empty/error/retry/conflict UX.

blockers.summary: The public frontend now fails closed without canned plans or payment mutation, but cannot represent live loading/empty/error/retry, eligibility, or activation-pending states.
blockers.resolution: Bind verified live projections and render explicit state machines; never treat service failure as free/no-plan, and restore payment mutation only through the separately authorized idempotent A6 flow.

blockers.summary: Pinned source behavior is the compatibility baseline, not complete production proof: manual activation is non-persistent, permission errors are swallowed, and monitor/switch writes are non-atomic.
blockers.resolution: Preserve externally relied-on contracts while replacing these internals with the verified state machine, transactions, outbox, and reconciliation before cutover.

blockers.summary: No subscription shadow-traffic, deploy, SLO, cutover, or rollback evidence exists.
blockers.resolution: Deploy behind routing flags, shadow compare, canary mutations, define stop triggers, and retain source authority until acceptance is met.

requiredExecutionOrder.acceptance: Versioned plan/subscription DTOs, status/envelope rules, owner keys, manual-renewal policy, and single plan authority are approved.
Reviewed additive migrations provide lifecycle, payment cause, constraints, idempotency, outbox/inbox, scheduler, audit, and reconciliation state; no startup DDL remains.
Restartable dry-run and apply modes reconcile subscriptions, wallet assignments, payments, permissions, and ranking with zero unexplained discrepancies.
User routes derive owner from verified JWT, foreign IDs return 404, internal events authenticate service identity, and canonical admin permissions pass negative tests.
Only finalized A6 events activate/extend once; amount/token/receiver/chain/plan version match and replay/crash tests pass.
Create/read/cancel/preview/switch/renew/expiry/grace state transitions are transactional, constrained, audited, and concurrency-tested.
Grant/revoke and ranking projections consume lifecycle events idempotently, fail truthfully, meet lag SLOs, and reconcile from cause history.
Source-compatible adapters and live owner/admin UX pass loading, empty, error, retry, forbidden, conflict, pending-finality, and success tests without canned production data.
Route/contract fixtures, lifecycle integration, shadow comparison, canary, observability, reconciliation, and rollback drill pass before source authority is disabled.
